decisions.reason: As a recently launched extension of the core authentication and secure communication offering, it fits the firm's announced cross-channel identity strategy and the sunk R&D and public website commitment make management likely to continue with it.

This mobile PDF digital signature function is close to the established offer and clearly supports the firm's move toward app-based interactions and online contract signing, so management would likely persist rather than reverse course after only one year.

A multi-layer end-to-end security architecture sits squarely in the firm's technical core, and given the firm's R&D intensity and public commitment, disappointing early traction would likely be treated as temporary rather than a reason to withdraw.
The secure email-to-app message delivery robot builds on the firm's trusted second-channel communication proposition, so its strategic fit and the resources already invested favor retention.

Although it is a specific hardware-oriented product, it remains close to the firm's security portfolio and leverages existing hardware and authentication capabilities, which makes escalation of commitment toward keeping it likely.

The payment network security compliance suite matches the firm's emphasis on strong, compliant security for sensitive transactions, so management would likely keep backing it in a growing market after its initial launch period.
